title: Benchmarks as Software: Terminal-Bench and the Case for Continuous Benchmarks
abstract: arXiv:2611.08417v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Coding agents are among the most economically consequential deployments of LLMs to date, making reliable evaluation increasingly important. Yet even benchmarks that are carefully validated at release can become stale. As models improve, they can discover valid solutions that existing verifiers reject, while changes to evaluation infrastructure can invalidate assumptions embedded in tasks and tests. We call the resulting accumulation of defects benchmark maintenance debt: a growing gap between benchmark scores and the capabilities they are intended to measure. We introduce a continuous-validation workflow for agentic benchmarks that combines community reports, task artifacts, agent traces, automated oracle checks, and human-gated repairs. We apply this workflow to Terminal-Bench 2.0, a benchmark that underwent extensive human and LM-assisted review and red-teaming before release. Our audit identifies issues in roughly 30% of the benchmark

translated_title: 基准测试即软件：Terminal-Bench与持续基准测试的论证
translated_abstract: 编程智能体是迄今为止大语言模型最具经济影响力的应用之一，这使得可靠的评估变得日益重要。然而，即使是发布时经过严格验证的基准测试也可能逐渐过时。随着模型能力的提升，它们可能找到被现有验证器拒绝的有效解决方案，而评估基础设施的变更也可能使任务和测试中固化的假设失效。我们将由此产生的缺陷累积称为“基准维护债务”：即基准测试分数与其原本想要衡量的能力之间不断扩大的差距。我们提出了一种针对智能体基准测试的持续验证工作流，该工作流结合了社区报告、任务工件、智能体轨迹、自动化标准答案检查以及由人工把关的修复机制。我们将该工作流应用于Terminal-Bench 2.0——一个在发布前经历了大量人工与语言模型辅助审查及红队测试的基准测试。我们的审计发现该基准测试中约30%的任务存在问题。
tldr: 论文提出“基准维护债务”概念，并构建了结合社区报告、自动检查与人工修复的持续验证工作流，对Terminal-Bench 2.0的审计发现约30%的任务存在缺陷，论证了基准测试应像软件一样进行持续维护。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces the concept of "benchmark maintenance debt" and proposes a continuous-validation workflow combining community reports, automated oracle checks, and human-gated repairs, with an audit of Terminal-Bench 2.0 revealing issues in roughly 30% of its tasks, arguing that benchmarks should be maintained like software.
